description: This bar chart, titled "How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary Perception," illustrates the popularity of three distinct knowledge domains—Movies, Songs, and Basketball—across five different evaluation conditions for large language models (LLMs). The vertical axis represents "Popularity" on a linear scale ranging from 20 to 220, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis categorizes the knowledge domains, presented in order from left to right as "Movies," "Songs," and "Basketball." For each domain, five bars are displayed, corresponding to the following conditions as indicated by the legend: "Llama3" (solid blue), "Qwen2" (solid red), "ChatGPT" (solid yellow), "Acc=0 & GT Ans" (cross-hatched blue), and "Acc=1 & GT Ans" (cross-hatched red). The bars are grouped by domain, with each group containing one bar per condition. The bars are not sorted by height; they are presented in the order specified by the legend for each group. The "Basketball" domain shows the highest overall popularity values, with the "Qwen2" (solid red) bar reaching approximately 215, the "Llama3" (solid blue) bar at approximately 180, and the "ChatGPT" (solid yellow) bar at approximately 170. The "Movies" domain shows the lowest popularity values, with all bars falling below 50, and the "Songs" domain shows intermediate values, with the "Qwen2" (solid red) bar reaching approximately 85. The cross-hatched bars ("Acc=0 & GT Ans" and "Acc=1 & GT Ans") are consistently shorter than their solid-colored counterparts for the same model, indicating lower popularity under those specific conditions. The bars are not visually emphasized beyond their color and pattern coding.
